Lymphopenia is observed in association with infections (i.e., viral or bacterial), autoimmune diseases, or advanced HIV infection. Inherited disorders, such as congenital neutropenia syndromes, Wiskott–Aldrich syndrome, and severe combined immunodeficiency disorder, are rare but may also cause leukopenia [5,40]. Treatment for leukopenia involves addressing the underlying cause.
